target_customer: Local brick and mortar businesses that wanted anonymous real-time customer feedback, paying per location per month
problem: Small local businesses had no easy channel to hear unfiltered complaints from customers while those customers were still in the store.
business_model: SaaS subscription per location (reported about 25 USD per month) with signage and a dedicated text number
product_category: Consumer to business messaging and feedback

founders.name: Qasar Younis
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO and as founder of Applied Intuition (a later company). No education or prior employer stated on the page I opened.

founders.name: Sunny Dhillon
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he built user-facing apps and managed teams of 35 plus across web, Android and iOS. The Google and Verily roles may include time after the TalkBin acquisition; the page does not date them.

founders.name: Michael Ma
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/COO on the YC page with no bio.

exit.reason: Terms were not disclosed. Google closed the product on 2014-07-31 citing dwindling usage.

technical_complexity.rationale: A texting gateway with per-location numbers plus iOS and Android apps was standard engineering for a small team in 2011; no hard research problem.

defensibility.rationale: The product was an SMS forwarding service with signage. Nothing proprietary stopped Yelp, Google or others from copying it, and the market need was unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google bought the company about five months after launch in April 2011, folded the team into mobile and local, then shut the product on 2014-07-31 after usage dwindled.

market_need_then: The founders pitched anonymous in-store feedback as a way for owners to fix problems before bad public reviews. At least one commentator in 2011 doubted there was much need for real-time anonymous feedback, and Google later cited dwindling usage.

branding.domain_note: Used talkbin.com; the site returned HTTP 503 when fetched in this session.

identity.visual_style: Physical signage with a TalkBin number was given to businesses; style not described

branding.community_and_virality: A trade blog noted a Google TalkBin sign spotted in San Francisco, which shows the signage reached the street; no wider community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself; the name was functional and the brand was absorbed into Google within five months.

outcome_analysis: TalkBin was acquired by Google in April 2011, roughly five months after launch, for an undisclosed sum, and its team joined mobile and local. The product itself did not last: Google shut it down on 2014-07-31 saying usage had dwindled, which suggests weak sustained demand for anonymous in-store feedback. The factor code other covers this since no code fits cleanly. The success factor recorded is only that the team was attractive enough to be bought early.
notes: No funding data found; dealroom and cbinsights pages did not show rounds. Company website returned 503. No dated competitor sources were found near the Winter 2011 batch; Tello (2012) launched later and is not a founding-time competitor. The Techcrunch 2011 acquisition article URL guessed returned 404 so the date comes from alltopstartups 2011-04-27 plus search summaries. Michael Ma appears on the YC page only.
